# How far a word reaches {#word-reach}

English often leaves it to guesswork how far a word reaches: in *I doubt Azozon said the dog runs*, only context tells whether you doubt the saying or the running. Ageben fixes it with a few rules you have already met one page at a time. Side by side, they say how far each kind of word reaches, which word covers which, what gets into a dependent, an island, or a quote, whose view each word gives, and what carries past a period.

### From one word to past the period {#reach-sizes}

When you read a sentence, the question to ask of each word is what it is about: the stretch of talk it is about is its **reach**. Each kind of word has one of five reaches, and its spelling and its place tell you which. Once you know the reach, you know what a word adds to the sentence and what it leaves alone.

| Reach | Words with that reach | Example | Taught in |
|-------|-----------------------|---------|-----------|
| One word | A tone mark written onto a word | `zazozon ?dodozel vayebel.` *Azozon saw a dog, I think* (unsure about just the dog) | [Tone marks](tone-marks.md#showing-your-tone) |
| A phrase | The binder inside an island's braces | `zazozon { hogugem zodozel gerulol } vayebel.` | [Scope islands](scope-islands.md#scope-islands) |
| A clause | A stance word, a channel, a feeling or sake word on `/th/`, an intention adverb | `thevemem zazozon vowurol xam zalazun veruvol.` doubts only the walking | [Which word covers which](/clause#which-covers-which), [clause joins](/joins#clause-joins) |
| The rest of the sentence | The act word; an *every* phrase or a newly mentioned noun, from its place onward; a bound tag | `zual godozel dogozel vayebel.` | [Speech acts](/speech-moves#speech-act-statement-question-command), [everything](/joins#everything-ua), [bound tags](universals-domains.md#bound-tags) |
| Past the period | A channel carried forward, the topic, what `-rth` and a hook on `-r` point back to | `zalazun thebam vudurul. zalazun veruvol.` | [Carrying a channel forward](evidentiality.md#carry-forward), [topic](topic.md#topic) |

A phrase with the reach of the rest of the sentence also reaches into the sentence a stand-in in it points to. Here `blarl` points to the next sentence, so the *every* phrase still reaches it, and `zogozer` there is each cat in turn:

> `zual gogozel vezuvel thahum blarl. zogozer guzemel.`
>
> [z-everything | g-cat] | v-sleep | [th-because | bl-that-clause] . z-←cat | g-sleepy
>
> "Every cat sleeps because it is sleepy." (each cat, because that cat is sleepy)

A clause-reach word stays in its clause even when another clause is joined to it. In `thevemem zazozon vowurol xam zalazun veruvol.` the doubt is only about Azozon walking, while the act word at the start of the turn reaches every clause of the join.

### Earlier covers later {#earlier-covers-later}

Two words that both reach the whole clause need an order: one is about the other. Ageben's general rule is that the earlier word covers the later one, so it is about the later word and the claim together. Their order alone sets this, so swapping two such words changes what you say.

> `thewemum thevemem zodozel vowurol.`
>
> th-concern | th-doubt | z-dog | v-walk
>
> "Worryingly, I doubt a dog is walking." (the doubt worries you)

> `thevemem thewemum zodozel vowurol.`
>
> th-doubt | th-concern | z-dog | v-walk
>
> "I doubt a dog is walking, worrying as that would be." (the walking would worry you)

An *every* phrase and a noun you mention for the first time take part in the same order, so moving one to the front chooses which covers which. In the first sentence below each dog may see a different cat; in the second there is one cat for all of them.

> `zual godozel dogozel vayebel.`
>
> [z-everything | g-dog] | d-cat | v-see
>
> "Every dog sees a cat." (each dog may see a different cat)

> `dogozel zual godozel vayebel.`
>
> d-cat | [z-everything | g-dog] | v-see
>
> "There is a cat that every dog sees." (one cat)

With only one such word, its place changes nothing, and an ordinary adverb of how, when, or where never takes part. The words below keep a rule of their own instead of text order. Most of these rules come from what the word does: an act word frames the whole turn, a remark is yours rather than part of the claim, and a holder owns its clause.

| Word | Its rule | Example | Taught in |
|------|----------|---------|-----------|
| The act word | First in its turn, so it covers the rest | `yel zazozon vowurol.` | [Speech acts](/speech-moves#speech-act-statement-question-command) |
| Two act words | The first is the act you really do and covers the second | `yol yel vabuvul dubogal zawan.` | [Stacking two act words](more-turn-words.md#stacked-acts) |
| A call | Changes nothing claimed, so it may sit before or after a stance word | `yalazun.` | [Call someone](/speech-moves#vocative) |
| A remark: your attitude, MIRATIVE, a sake word on the clause, `uom` with its stance | Stays yours and outside what is asked, though the act word comes first | `yel zazozon vowurol thobatham.` | [Attitudes](feelings.md#speaker-attitude), [it turns out](mirative.md#mirative), [whose stake](for-a-sake.md#whose-stake), [contrary to](contrary-to.md#contrary-to-stance) |
| A stance after `uom` | Only that stance is what the event goes against; a stance anywhere else in the clause still applies to the claim | `zazozon vowurol uom thagom thomam.` | [Contrary to](contrary-to.md#contrary-to-stance) |
| A channel | Never under your attitude, your surprise, or a cause, wherever it sits: it backs the whole claim | `theyom thahum blarl` | [Evidence clause](evidentiality.md#evidence-clause) |
| The seam word of a holder | Covers its whole clause, wherever it sits | `zalazun theyomazozon vudurul.` | [What belongs to the holder](holder.md#what-the-holder-covers) |
| A *because* or *if* hinge | Keeps its clause last, so the words before it cover it | `zazozon vowurol thohem blerulal.` | [If](/causation#if) |
| A `/th/` join right after stance words | Works only on those stance words | `zazozon vowurol thomam thul.` | [How far a stance join reaches](verb-and-stance-joins.md#stance-join-reach) |
| FORMER with a restrictor such as `hual` | Covers the restrictor though it comes after it | `zazozon hual vozuyel helam.` | [A pattern that used to hold](residue-and-former.md#former-climate) |

So when you meet two clause-reach words, check this table first, and fall back on text order only when neither word is in it.

### What gets into a box {#boxes}

Some stretches of a sentence keep words apart from the sentence around them: a clause in a join, a dependent after a stand-in, an island in braces, a quote, and an aside. Call each of these a **box**. Each kind of box sets two things: which outside words reach in, and whether words inside reach out. Knowing it tells you, for example, that your doubt about a report is never a doubt about the reported words.

| Box | Written | Reaches in | Stays out |
|-----|---------|------------|-----------|
| A clause in a join | `… xam …` | The act word; an *every* phrase or bound tag from earlier in the sentence; a channel carried from an earlier sentence | A stance word, a channel, or a holder in another clause |
| A dependent | after `darl`, `blarl`, and the other stand-ins | The holder of the clause around it; an *every* phrase or bound tag; a carried channel | Your act word and your stance words in the main sentence |
| An island | `{ … }` | Everything that reaches the clause | Nothing; the island's binder reaches only the island |
| A quote | `d[…]` | Nothing | Everything in your sentence: the quote keeps its own act word, tone mark, and frame |
| An aside | `th(…)` | Only a pronoun or other pointer back to earlier words | Everything else, and nothing in the aside reaches out |

A dependent only fills a role, so the words that frame the main sentence are about the main claim, not about the inner sentence ([dependent clauses](/dependents#dependent-clauses)):

> `thevemem zazozon vezuyol balazun darl zodozel veruvol.`
>
> th-doubt | z-Azozon | v-tell | b-Alazun | d-that-clause | z-dog | v-run
>
> "I doubt Azozon tells Alazun that the dog runs." (you doubt the telling; you say nothing about the dog)

A holder is the one frame of the main clause that does reach a dependent: it covers its clause and any dependent sentence inside it ([what belongs to the holder](holder.md#what-the-holder-covers)). An *every* phrase and a bound tag reach into the sentence a stand-in points to as well ([bound tags](universals-domains.md#bound-tags)).

A quote is closed both ways. Your act word and stance words are about your claim that the words were said, and a quoted question keeps its own `yel` ([act words in a quote](quote-contents.md#quote-acts)):

> `thevemem zazozon d[zalazun vowurol] vezuyol.`
>
> th-doubt | z-Azozon | d-CITE[z-Alazun | v-walk] | v-tell
>
> "I doubt Azozon said, “Alazun walks.”" (you doubt the saying, not the walking)

An aside takes its own act word, and a question in it is one you wonder aloud, so a reply answers the outer sentence ([asides](/spans#asides-th)):

> `zazozon vowurol th(yel zalazun vezuvel).`
>
> z-Azozon | v-walk | th-ASIDE[y-question | z-Alazun | v-sleep]
>
> "Azozon walks (is Alazun asleep?)."

A carried channel is the reverse case: it covers everything your later statement claims, every clause of a join and the dependents and islands inside it included, but never a quote ([carrying a channel forward](evidentiality.md#carry-forward)).

### Whose it is {#whose-it-is}

Besides how far a word reaches, each word belongs to someone: you, the holder whose view the clause gives, or, in a question, the listener you ask. The owner decides what the listener can agree or disagree with. A word that is yours stays yours wherever it sits; only the words of the claim go to a holder or into the question.

| Owner | Words | Taught in |
|-------|-------|-----------|
| You | The act word, pronouns, your attitudes and remarks, a sake word with no holder, and the seam word itself, which says how you know the holder's view | [What belongs to the holder](holder.md#what-the-holder-covers), [attitudes](feelings.md#speaker-attitude) |
| The holder | The rest of the clause: the event, MAY, CAUSE hinges and *so that*, plans, another channel, and sake and feeling words wherever they sit; a dependent inside the clause | [What belongs to the holder](holder.md#what-the-holder-covers), [someone else's plan, aim, or motive](holder.md#holder-plans-and-motives) |
| The one asked | In a question, only the claim; a channel in a question asks about the listener's grounds | [Whose stake](for-a-sake.md#whose-stake), [carrying a channel forward](evidentiality.md#carry-forward) |

The seam word covers a sake word in its clause whether the sake word comes before it or after it. Here the motive comes first and is still Azozon's, and the seam word says how you know Azozon's reason:

> `zazozon vezuyol thawethom theyomazozon.`
>
> z-Azozon | v-tell | th-relatedness-motive-any-term | th-CLUES-Azozon
>
> "I gather Azozon talks to feel connected."

A dependent with a seam word of its own switches the holder for that sentence only. So one sake word can be yours and another the holder's in the same stretch:

> `wawethum goyom zarl zalazun wawethum goyom theyomazozon.`
>
> [w-relatedness-unmet-modifiable | g-stimulus] | z-that-clause | [z-Alazun | [w-relatedness-unmet-modifiable | g-stimulus]] | th-CLUES-Azozon
>
> "It sits badly with me that, as I gather, Alazun sits badly with Azozon."

In a question, your remarks stay outside what is asked, so the listener answers only the claim. In `yel zazozon vowurol uom thagom.` the listener says whether Azozon walks, and nothing about your plan ([contrary to](contrary-to.md#contrary-to-stance)).

> `yel themem vowurol zazozon.`
>
> y-question | th-MIRATIVE | v-walk | z-Azozon
>
> "Is Azozon walking, of all things?"

### What carries past a period {#past-the-period}

Most words stop at the period. An *every* phrase and a bound tag end with their sentence, though they reach on into the sentences a stand-in in that stretch points to, and a call closed by a period reaches only its own turn ([what carries past a period](sentence-linkers.md#past-a-period)). A few things do carry on, each until a set event ends it, and knowing those events tells you when a later sentence still depends on an earlier one.

| What carries | Read by | Ends with | Taught in |
|--------------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| Your frame: a channel, a holder, or NOTIONAL | Your later statements with no channel of their own; never someone else's | A new frame, a written statement word (`yal`, `yam`, `yar`), *by the way* (`xavedam`), a goodbye | [Carrying a channel forward](evidentiality.md#carry-forward), [naming a holder](holder.md#naming-a-holder), [as if](notional.md#notional-as-if-framing) |
| The topic | A topic pronoun, by either speaker | A new topic or a return, *next* or *by the way*, a goodbye | [Topic](topic.md#topic) |
| The latest content of each kind | A stand-in on `-rth`, by either speaker | Newer content of that kind, a goodbye | [Pointing back](stand-in-vowels.md#stand-in-back) |
| The latest landmark | A hook on `-r`, by either speaker | A new landmark, a goodbye | [Point back](in-clause-hooks.md#hook-resume) |
| The sentence before | A sentence linker, a discourse hook, or a polar word, whoever said that sentence | The next sentence, a goodbye | [What carries past a period](sentence-linkers.md#past-a-period) |
| A question's blank | The sentence right after the question | Any other sentence, a reply that opens with *by the way*, a goodbye | [Fill-ask](/questions#fill-ask) |

A frame applies only to statements. A question neither takes it nor ends it, so it applies again to your next statement:

> `zalazun thebam vudurul. yel zalazun veruvol. zalazun vozuyel.`
>
> z-Alazun | th-REPORTED | v-departure . y-question | z-Alazun | v-run . z-Alazun | v-sing
>
> "Alazun left, so they say. Did Alazun run? Alazun sang." (the singing is hearsay too)

A written statement word ends your frame, but it ends nothing else in the table: the topic, `-rth`, a hook on `-r`, and the sentence before all go on past `yal`. A reply that opens with any statement word still fills the blank, so you can hedge an answer with `yam` or `yar`:

> `yel zar vowurol. yam azozon.`
>
> y-question | z-wh | v-walk . y-soft-statement | Azozon
>
> "Who walks?" "Azozon, I think."

A goodbye ends the conversation, so everything in the table ends there for the sentences after it, whoever says it and whatever was set before. A quote also begins with nothing carried in: inside it, `-rth` and a hook on `-r` point back only within the quoted words, and your frame does not carry in.

### Practice {#intermediate-practice}

Short drills for Intermediate. Try each item before opening **Show answer**.

**Setting:** a ski slope

**New words:**

| English | Ageben | Cue |
|---------|--------|-----|
| *ski* | `uzunol` | ⛷️ |
| *snowboard* | `ozunol` | 🏂 |
| *goggles* | `egebul` | 🥽 |
| *snowman* | `ozalel` | ☃️ |
| *concern* | `thewemum` | 😟 from *worried* |

**Review:**

| English | Ageben |
|---------|--------|
| *Azozon* | `azozon` |
| *Alazun* | `alazun` |
| *Ahelan* | `ahelan` |
| *person* | `eyel` |
| *doubt* | `thevemem` |
| *CLUES* | `theyom` |
| *REPORTED* | `thebam` |
| *see* | `vayebel` |
| *tell* | `vezuyol` |
| *sleep* | `vezuvel` |

#### English → Ageben {#intermediate-english-to-ageben}

**1.** *Azozon saw goggles, I think.* (only the goggles are a guess)

::: details Show answer
`zazozon ?degebul vayebel.`

z-Azozon | ?d-goggles | v-see
:::

**2.** *I doubt Ahelan told Azozon that Alazun skis.* (you doubt the telling)

::: details Show answer
`thevemem zahelan vezuyol bazozon darl zalazun vuzunol.`

th-doubt | z-Ahelan | v-tell | b-Azozon | d-that-clause | z-Alazun | v-ski
:::

**3.** *I doubt Alazun skis, and Azozon snowboards.* (only the skiing is in doubt)

::: details Show answer
`thevemem zalazun vuzunol xam zazozon vozunol.`

[th-doubt | z-Alazun | v-ski | x-and.open | z-Azozon | v-snowboard]
:::

**4.** *I gather Alazun skis to feel connected.* (the motive is Alazun's)

::: details Show answer
`zalazun vuzunol thawethom theyomalazun.`

z-Alazun | v-ski | th-relatedness-motive-any-term | th-CLUES-Alazun

**Also correct:** `zalazun theyomalazun vuzunol thawethom.`
:::

#### Ageben → English {#intermediate-ageben-to-english}

**1.** `zalazun vuzunol th(yel zahelan vezuvel).`

::: details Show answer
z-Alazun | v-ski | th-ASIDE[y-question | z-Ahelan | v-sleep]

*Alazun skis (is Ahelan asleep?).*
:::

**2.** `thevemem zazozon d[zahelan vozunol] vezuyol.`

::: details Show answer
th-doubt | z-Azozon | d-CITE[z-Ahelan | v-snowboard] | v-tell

*I doubt Azozon said, “Ahelan snowboards.”* (you doubt the saying, not the snowboarding)
:::

**3.** `yel themem vuzunol zazozon.`

::: details Show answer
y-question | th-MIRATIVE | v-ski | z-Azozon

*Is Azozon skiing, of all things?*
:::

**4.** `yel zar vozunol. yam azozon.`

::: details Show answer
y-question | z-wh | v-snowboard . y-soft-statement | Azozon

*“Who is snowboarding?” “Azozon, I think.”*
:::

#### Pick one {#intermediate-pick-one}

**1.** *I doubt Alazun skis, worrying as that would be.* `thevemem thewemum zalazun vuzunol.` or `thewemum thevemem zalazun vuzunol.`

::: details Show answer
`thevemem thewemum zalazun vuzunol.`

th-doubt | th-concern | z-Alazun | v-ski

The earlier word covers the later one: doubt first puts the worry under the doubt, on the skiing.
:::

#### Fix it {#intermediate-fix-it}

**1.** *There is one snowman that everyone sees.* <!-- lint: error -->`zual geyel dozalel vayebel.`

::: details Show answer
`dozalel zual geyel vayebel.`

d-snowman | [z-everything | g-person] | v-see

English order puts *everyone* first, which lets each person see a different snowman; the snowman goes first to be one for all.
:::

#### What changes {#intermediate-what-changes}

**1.** `zalazun thebam vozunol. yel zahelan vuzunol. zazozon vozunol.` / `zalazun thebam vozunol. yal zahelan vuzunol. zazozon vozunol.`

::: details Show answer
z-Alazun | th-REPORTED | v-snowboard . y-question | z-Ahelan | v-ski . z-Azozon | v-snowboard

z-Alazun | th-REPORTED | v-snowboard . y-statement | z-Ahelan | v-ski . z-Azozon | v-snowboard

In the first, the question skips the hearsay, so Azozon snowboarding is hearsay too. In the second, `yal` ends it: Ahelan skiing and Azozon snowboarding are your own claims.
:::
